title: Marked square-zero algebra extensions and their classes
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a map of commutative rings and let $N$ be a $B$-module. A marked square-zero extension consists of a commutative $R$-algebra $E$, a surjective $R$-algebra map $p:E\to B$, and an injective additive map $i:N\to E$ with image $\ker p$, such that $i(n)i(m)=0$ and $x i(n)=i(p(x)n)$. An isomorphism of extensions is an $R$-algebra isomorphism commuting with $p$ and $i$. Define $\operatorname{Exal}_R(B,N)$ as the quotient by extension isomorphisms. Write $[E]$ for the class of an extension. For extensions $E,F,G$, the Baer-sum relation holds if there is an $R$-algebra map $b:E\times_B F\to G$ over $B$ carrying $(i_E(n),i_F(m))$ to $i_G(n+m)$. For $a\in R$, the scalar-pushout relation between $E,F$ holds if there is an $R$-algebra map $E\to F$ over $B$ carrying $i_E(n)$ to $i_F(an)$. An abelian group and $R$-module structure on the class set is natural if $[E]+[F]=[G]$ holds exactly for the Baer-sum relation and $a[E]=[F]$ holds exactly for the scalar-pushout relation. These are the operation graphs; this definition does not assert existence of the module structure.
